questions.question: If the ball, delivered by the bowler, not being a Wide, passes the striker without touching his/her bat or person, any runs completed by the batters from that delivery, or a boundary allowance, shall be credited as _________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Byes**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In cricket,
 
 
• **byes** are runs that the batting team can score when the ball passes the batter without hitting their bat or body, and the fielders are unable to gather the ball in time to prevent the batsmen from completing the runs.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__** 

 
• Some other Cricket Terminologies
 
 
• **The Delivery**:

 
 
• A bowler delivers a ball that is not wide (it is within the acceptable range for the batter to play).
 
 
 
• **The Ball Passes the Batter**:
 
 
• If the ball passes the batter without touching their bat or person (such as their gloves, body, or pad), it is considered "not hit."
 
• This can happen if the batter misses the ball or if it is a legitimate delivery but the batter is not able to make contact.
 
 
 
• **Runs Scored**:
 
 
• If the batter and their partner run between the wickets during this delivery, these runs are counted as **byes**, not leg runs or any other type of runs. The reason for this is that the runs are completed despite the batter not making contact with the ball, which distinguishes byes from other types of runs, such as leg byes (which occur when the ball touches the batter's body).
 
 
 
• **Boundary Allowance**:
 
 
• If the ball crosses the boundary without being touched by any fielder (whether due to the batter missing or the ball being played in a way that no fielder can intercept it), the batsmen would be credited with a boundary (four or six), and this would also be added to the total score as **byes**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• His extraordinary goal-scoring ability earned him the nickname "The Wizard" or "The Magician of Hockey."
 
• He played a pivotal role in securing gold medals for India in the 1928, 1932, and 1936 Olympics.
 
 
 
• **Indian Hockey Team's Olympic Success**
 
 
• India's men's hockey team has won a total of eight Olympic gold medals (1928, 1932, 1936, 1948, 1952, 1956, 1964, 1980).
 
• The team set an Olympic record by winning six consecutive gold medals from 1928 to 1956.
 
 
 
• **Field Hockey in the Olympics**
 
 
• Field hockey has been a part of the Summer Olympics since 1908 for men and 1980 for women.

questions.question: In Badminton, the length and width of the doubles court shall be of ______________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**13.40 m × 6.10 m**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• 13.40 m × 6.10m is the official dimension for badminton doubles court.
 
• The length of the court is 13.40 meters, and the width is 6.10 meters.
 
• These dimensions are set by the Badminton World Federation (BWF) and are followed in all official tournaments.
 
• The court has a center line that divides it into two equal halves, and there are service boxes marked on both sides.
 
• The net is placed in the center, and its height is 1.55 meters at the edges and 1.524 meters in the center.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

**Badminton Overview:**

 
• Sport Type: Racquet sport played using racquets to hit a shuttlecock across a net.
 
• Team Members: Can be played as singles (one player per side) or doubles (two players per side).
 
• Equipment: Shuttlecock and racquet.
 
• Playing Area: Played on a rectangular indoor court.
 
• Objective: Points are scored by hitting the shuttlecock with the racquet and making it land within the opponent's half of the court.
 
• Shuttlecock: A feathered or plastic projectile that decelerates rapidly due to its design.
 
• Origin: Developed in British India from the earlier game of battledore and shuttlecock. Became popular in Asia, especially in China.
 
• Olympic Debut: Introduced in the Summer Olympics in 1992 with events like men's singles, women's singles, men's doubles, and women's doubles. Mixed doubles was added later.
 
• Physical Demands: Requires aerobic stamina, agility, strength, speed, and precision. It's also a technical sport demanding good motor coordination.

**Court Dimensions:**

 
• Full Width: 6.1 metres (20 feet) for doubles and 5.18 metres (17.0 feet) for singles.
 
• Full Length: 13.4 metres (44 feet).
 
• Net Height: 1.55 metres (5 feet 1 inch) at the edges and 1.524 metres (5.00 feet) in the center.

questions.question: How many events are there in decathlon?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**10**__.

__
 
• **Decathlon **is a combined event in athletics **consisting of ten track and field events.**
 
• The events in decathlon are **100 meters**, **400 meters**,**1500 meters**, **110 meters** of **hurdles**,** ****long jump**, **shot put**, **high jump**, **discus throw**, **pole vault**, and** javelin throw.**
 
• The pentathlon events that took place at the **ancient Greek Olympics** gave rise to the decathlon.
 
• Pentathlons comprised five events: sprint, discus throw, javelin throw, long jump, and wrestling battle.
 
• This **competition was first held at Olympia in 708 BC**, and for many centuries it was incredibly popular.
 
• The **modern decathlon** made its **debut **in the **Olympic athletics **schedule during the **Stockholm Games in 1912.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

questions.question: In case of first false start in a running event, the athlete(s) shall be ___________.
questions.solution:

• The** new rule has been successful in reducing the number of false starts, and races are now able to start and finish more quickly.**
